Note on Methodology

Shift is measured as change in average % score across attempted subjects, limited to students who attempted at least 3 subjects in both tests — so a shift reflects real performance change, not absenteeism.

Integrated Action Plan

From the combined subject & student-level analysis
  • 1Subject level: Immediate intervention needed in Physics and Chemistry, where failure rates exceed 50% — focus on foundational numerical problem-solving.
  • 2Peer tutoring: Pair the 11 consistent Biology toppers with students in the critical support cohort for structured study groups.
  • 3Remedial re-tests: Schedule focused revision and re-assessment for the 14 students in the critical support list.
  • 4Drop investigation: Follow up individually with high-drop students (e.g. Kaviraj, Aditya, Aashritha) to identify specific Test 2 syllabus gaps.
  • 5Curriculum review: Investigate what changed between Test 1 and Test 2 syllabus coverage that produced the widespread score drop in July.

Biology's Edge, Side by Side

How Biology compares across both assessment types
MetricSlip Tests (Combined)Monthly Test

Why Biology Leads

  • 1Biology posts the highest average score of any subject in both the Slip Tests (58.9% combined) and the Monthly Test (70.8%).
  • 2Biology has the lowest failure rate among core subjects in both assessments — 15.05% combined in Slip Tests, and just 5 failures (out of 80 who appeared) in the Monthly Test.
  • 3Biology shows the highest topper density — 27.96% scoring >15/20 in Slip Tests, and 25 students (the most of any subject) scoring 35+/40 in the Monthly Test.
  • 4Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics consistently show failure rates above 25–55% across both assessment types — the gap with Biology is structural, not a one-test effect.
